children: US sugar futures extended their downward trend to trade around 18.5 cents per pound, the lowest since September, driven by a combination of a weaker Brazilian real, continued fund selling and lower oil prices.
Expectations of greater supply from India added to the bearish sentiment.

According to a major industry body, sugar production in the world's second-largest producer jumped by 745% yoy to 845,000 in October, as mills in Maharashtra brought forward the start of the crushing season to build stocks ahead of the festive period.
However, supply developments in Brazil offered a contrasting picture.
Sugarcane crushing and sugar production fell during the first half of October, as heavy rainfall across the Center-South disrupted harvesting and delayed mill operations.
The weather-related disruption could persist, with the early impact of El Niño raising concerns over the pace of harvesting and the start of the next crushing season.

title: Sugar Futures at Over 1-Month Low
